issue.title: Hidden subcommands (monitor _supervise, tool _adopt) still show as '==SUPPRESS==' rows in group --help
issue.description:
Found by the sase-17p land agent (2026-09-24, master 682089c84, Python 3.14 venv).

Hidden internal subcommands registered with `subparsers.add_parser(NAME,
help=argparse.SUPPRESS)` are still listed in their group's help, with the literal
placeholder text:

    $ sase monitor --help
      {list,show,resume,start,stop}
        _supervise          ==SUPPRESS==
    $ sase tool --help
      {list,run,runs,show,stop,wait}
        _adopt              ==SUPPRESS==

The explicit `metavar=` on the subparsers action keeps them out of the usage line and the
`{...}` choice list, but argparse still creates a `_ChoicesPseudoAction` row for every
`add_parser(..., help=...)` call and renders `==SUPPRESS==` as its help text. The
existing tests only assert the usage line and the `{...}` string (see
tests/main/test_parser_monitor.py::test_monitor_group_help_lists_sorted_visible_subcommands
and tests/main/test_parser_tool.py::test_tool_help_advertises_implemented_verbs), so
they miss the row.

Fix: one shared parser helper that registers a hidden subcommand without a help row.
Either omit `help=` and drop the pseudo action from the subparsers action's
`_choices_actions`, or filter SUPPRESS rows in the shared help formatter. Use it for
`monitor _supervise` and `tool _adopt`, and audit the other `help=argparse.SUPPRESS`
add_parser calls. Extend both help tests to assert that no `==SUPPRESS==` text and no
hidden verb appear anywhere in the group help.

task_type_fields.impact: Cosmetic but user-facing: every group help advertises internal worker entry points and a raw argparse sentinel string.
task_type_fields.repro: Run 'sase monitor --help' or 'sase tool --help' and look at the subcommand rows: '_supervise ==SUPPRESS==' / '_adopt ==SUPPRESS==' are listed.
